description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and the accuracy (ACC, %) (y-axis) for five different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, and MEMIT—evaluated on long-tail biomedical knowledge editing in large language models. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” spans from 0 to 10⁴ on a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 60% to 80% on a linear scale, with tick marks at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The “Base” method (black line with circular markers) shows a steady increase from approximately 61% at co-occurrence 1 to 67% at 10⁴. The “FT” method (blue line with downward-pointing triangular markers) starts at ~63% and rises to ~68.5%. The “IKE” method (red line with upward-pointing triangular markers) begins at ~64.5% and reaches ~70%. The “MEND” method (brown line with diamond markers) starts at ~66.5% and climbs to ~74%. The “MEMIT” method (purple line with circular markers) begins at ~66.5% and increases to ~72.5%. All methods show a positive trend in accuracy as co-occurrence number increases, with MEND consistently achieving the highest performance across the range, followed by MEMIT, IKE, FT, and Base. A gray rectangular legend entry labeled “MEMIT” appears in the top right but does not correspond to a plotted line, likely indicating a labeling artifact.
